items.detail: An RFC becomes requirements, grammars, layouts, registries, defined procedures and limits, each with a source span and a digest (design D1).
items.label: The catalogue, rfcspec/1

items.detail: Machines lower to ess-protospec/1, message and value types and registries to an ess/N system; what ESS cannot carry is listed as a gap (design D2).
items.label: ESS as the target

items.detail: Bytes and bits live in rfcspec-wire/1: ABNF verbatim, bit-level ABNF and packet layouts (design D3).
items.label: A wire-format sidecar

items.detail: One value per axis for each protocol layer: unit, delivery, direction, multiplexing, exchange, correlation, lifetime, layering, roles (design D4).
items.label: Communication semantics

items.detail: Model output is a recorded proposal with cited spans, replayed offline; no gate calls a model (design D5, D6).
items.label: AI proposes, review decides

items.detail: Wire protocols, data formats, extensions and registries are modelled; algorithms as signatures with test vectors; the rest get a requirement catalogue (design D11).
items.label: Which kinds of RFC are modelled

items.detail: RFC 6455 from plain text and RFC 9220 from RFCXML: sections, requirements, ABNF and defined terms; a survey classifying every RFC in the index by kind.
items.label: Fetch, read and extract

items.detail: The RFC 6455 handshake grammar and frame bit-level ABNF and diagram, an agreement check between them, and a generated codec with round-trip and mutation vectors.
items.label: ABNF and the wire layer

items.detail: Recorded proposals for parties, semantics and the WebSocket machines, overlay review, and lowering that ess specify validate and ess protocol explore accept.
items.label: Proposals, review and lowering

items.detail: A generated sans-IO Rust crate with codec, machine, limits and roles, an Autobahn run and the requirement matrix.
items.label: A generated WebSocket core

items.detail: DNS over UDP: binary layouts, correlation by id, concurrent sessions; the ESS gap proposals with WebSocket and DNS as evidence.
items.label: A second, binary protocol

items.detail: The WebSocket codec as a pure WASM module and a websocket channel port in a Spindle environment.
items.label: RFCspec cores in Spindle

items.detail: TCP as the hard case: sequence-number arithmetic, windows and timers from measurements.
items.label: A transport
